boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Sailor's Creek record (April 6, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. The record includes the separate actions against Ewell and Anderson and the Second Corps' fight with Gordon at Perkinson's mill (the frozen other names include Lockett Farm); Rice's Station (VA092) and High Bridge (VA095) are the same day. Humphreys commanded the Second Corps, and his account of its actions here is a participant's. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero. Humphreys gives Ewell about 3,600 and Anderson about 6,300 on the ground (about 10,000), built from Kershaw's 2,000, Custis Lee's about 1,000 (from Howard's paper), Johnson's division of about 3,800 and Pickett's of about 2,500, and relays Ewell's 'only about 3.000'. Ewell says his two divisions numbered about 3,000 each at the evacuation, lost over 3,000 to fatigue on the march, and was told at Wright's headquarters that 30,000 men were engaged against them.
claims.rationale: Humphreys' figures are his reconstruction from mixed sources; Ewell's are strengths at the April 2 evacuation and a reported Union figure. Gordon's corps is not counted in either. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Ewell says Anderson's assault was repulsed in five minutes and that his whole command was captured; Humphreys says all of Ewell's command was killed, wounded or captured except 250 of Kershaw's division, and that Gordon fell back from the high ground beyond the creek at Perkinson's mill.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 9,980 total and the live field 8,848 (US 1,148; CS 7,700). Humphreys estimates Ewell's loss at about 3,400 and Anderson's at about 2,600 (about 6,000), the day's total Confederate loss at not less than 8,000, the Second Corps' captures at 13 flags, 4 guns and 1,700 prisoners, its own killed and wounded at 311 (First and Second divisions) and the Sixth Corps' at 442, and gives no cavalry figure. Ewell says 2,800 of his men were taken prisoner and about 150 killed and wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' components are his estimates from mixed sources; he gives 3 guns at the Perkinson's mill stand and 4 in the corps' captures.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
